question: A ladder 10.6 m long is leaning against a wall. It makes an angle of 30° with the ground. How high does the ladder reach on the wall?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **30°-60°-90° triangle**, the side opposite to 30° is always half of the **hypotenuse**.

Height = Hypotenuse ÷ 2

Height = 10.6 ÷ 2 = 5.3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 5.3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/df46d3e610acc0cf7b58c0da8a9a0b3a423f9646ffa5d7baf4565311d0c9ece5.png] 

**Given:**

Length of the **ladder** (Hypotenuse AC) = 10.6 m

Angle with the ground (θ) = 30°

**Formula Used:**

sin θ = Perpendicular / Hypotenuse

**Calculations:**

⇒ sin 30° = height / 10.6

⇒ 1 / 2 = height / 10.6

⇒ height = 10.6 × (1 / 2)

⇒ height = 5.3 m

**∴ The correct answer is 5.3 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios for 30°

sin 30° = 1/2, cos 30° = √3/2, and tan 30° = 1/√3.

Special Right Triangles

In a 30-60-90 triangle, the sides are in the ratio 1 : √3 : 2 corresponding to the angles.

Pythagoras Theorem

For any right-angled triangle, Base² + Perpendicular² = Hypotenuse².</p
